title: Capacity of parallel Gaussian channels via water-filling

problemStatement.formal: For noise powers N_1,...,N_n > 0 and budget P >= 0, max_{P_i >= 0, sum P_i <= P} sum_i (1/2) log(1 + P_i/N_i) = sum_i (1/2) log(1 + P_i*/N_i), attained by the water-filling allocation P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+ where the water level mu >= 0 is the unique solution of sum_i (mu - N_i)_+ = P.
problemStatement.plain: Given several independent noisy channels with noise levels N_i and a fixed total transmit power P to share among them, how should the power be split to maximise total data rate? The optimal answer is water-filling: pour power into a landscape whose floor heights are the noise levels until it reaches a common surface level mu, giving each channel power (mu - N_i)_+ and starving channels too noisy to be worth using. The task is to prove this allocation is optimal and that mu is uniquely fixed by the power budget.
whyMatters: Water-filling is the canonical resource-allocation result of information theory and underlies practical multicarrier bit-loading (OFDM/DMT) in DSL, Wi-Fi and 4G/5G.
It is the multi-channel completion of the scalar Shannon-Hartley formula already in the gallery, and formalising it exercises constrained concave (KKT/Lagrange) optimisation in Lean.

proven: Per-use AWGN capacity (1/2) log(1 + P/N) nats/use, verified axiom-free (gallery: shannon-channel-coding-awgn).
Bandlimited Shannon-Hartley C = B log2(1 + P/N) bits/s and its structural theory (gallery: shannon-channel-coding-awgn-oq-03), which explicitly defers this parallel-channel case.
The water-filling theorem is classical (Shannon 1949; Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Thm 9.9.1); only the Lean formalization is open.
open: A Lean 4 proof that P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+ maximises the parallel-channel rate under sum P_i <= P.
Existence and uniqueness of the water level mu solving sum_i (mu - N_i)_+ = P.
The closed-form optimum C = sum_i (1/2) log(max(mu, N_i)/N_i).
knownResults.goal: Formalize the finite-dimensional water-filling theorem: define the parallel-channel rate over a finite family N_1,...,N_n, prove existence/uniqueness of the water level, prove KKT optimality of P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+, and derive the closed-form capacity. Scope is the finite optimisation statement; the continuous infinite-band limit is a separate follow-up.

insights: Water-filling KKT optimality has a fully ELEMENTARY proof: the first-order condition is replaced by the per-channel tangent bound log u <= u-1 (Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos), summed across channels. No differentiability/Lagrange/KKT machinery needed.

Key identity N_i + (mu-N_i)_+ = max mu N_i turns the derivative coefficient 1/(2(N_i+P_i*)) into 1/(2 max(mu,N_i)), which is constant 1/(2mu) on ACTIVE channels (N_i<mu) and <= 1/(2mu) on inactive ones (P_i*=0, x_i>=0). This case split is exactly what makes the aggregated linear term collapse to (sum x_i - P)/(2mu) <= 0.

Water level existence = IVT on the continuous monotone budget g(mu)=sum (mu-N_i)_+ between g(0)=0 and g(N_{i0}+P)>=P; uniqueness (for P>0) = strict monotonicity of g wherever g>0 (some channel active).

VERIFIED (researcher-2, 2026-07-09, GREEN build attempt 1): capacity properties of the equal-noise closed form C(P)=(n/2)log(1+P/(nc)) in ShannonChannelCodingAWGNOQ03OQ01EqualNoise.lean. rate_equalNoise_nonneg (C(P)≥0 for P≥0, via Real.log_nonneg on 1≤1+P/(nc) + mul_nonneg) and rate_equalNoise_mono_power (P₁≤P₂⟹C(P₁)≤C(P₂), via Real.log_le_log + gcongr for the argument monotonicity). Standard 'capacity is a nonneg increasing function of the power budget' facts, absent from the file. The three parent open items (optimality, water-level existence/uniqueness, closed form) + equal-noise specialization are all complete; remaining nextSteps (operational random-coding theorem, infinite-band integral limit) are substantial.

The four separately-proved water-filling facts (existence, positivity, optimality, closed form) compose directly into the single "parallel Gaussian channel capacity is achieved by water-filling" statement — no new analysis needed, only the μ>0 bridge lemma.

Wideband/infinite-bandwidth AWGN limit: as the channel count n→∞, the equal-noise capacity (n/2)·log(1+P/(nc)) converges to EXACTLY P/(2c). Proof rewrites n·log(1+P/(nc)) = log((1+(P/c)/n)^n) via Real.log_pow (unconditional, no sign hyp on P), then applies Real.tendsto_one_add_div_pow_exp ((1+t/n)^n → exp t) composed with continuity of Real.log at exp(P/c)>0 and log∘exp=id, finally scaling by 1/2. No differentiability of log(1+x)/x needed — the (1+t/n)^n→exp form sidesteps the 0/0 tangent limit.

Sharpness of the wideband ceiling: rate_equalNoise_le_wideband gives C_n ≤ P/(2c) for every finite n, and rate_equalNoise_tendsto_wideband shows the sequence attains P/(2c) in the limit — so P/(2c) is exactly the supremum of achievable equal-noise rates, closing the finite-bound/limit pair.

The general water-filling capacity is jointly CONCAVE in the power vector on the nonnegative orthant (parallelRate_concaveOn_power): each per-channel ½log(1+Pᵢ/Nᵢ) is concave in its own coordinate (log∘affine), and a finite sum of concave functions on a common convex set is concave. This is the structural reason the water-filling allocation is a GLOBAL optimum — the feasible set {P≥0, ∑Pᵢ≤Pₜₒₜ} is convex and the objective is concave, so power allocation is a convex program.  Existing gallery concavity (rate_equalNoise_concaveOn_power) covered only the scalar equal-noise special case.

The wideband ceiling P/(2c) is the EXACT SUPREMUM (least upper bound), not merely the n→∞ limit, of the equal-noise rates over the channel count: ⨆ n:ℕ, (n/2)·log(1+P/(nc)) = P/(2c) for c>0, P≥0 (rate_equalNoise_iSup_eq_wideband). No monotonicity in n needed — the LUB drops out of the tendsto+ceiling pair alone: the per-n ceiling makes P/(2c) an upper bound (⨆ ≤ P/(2c) via ciSup_le), while the wideband limit forces the ⨆ up (P/(2c) = lim R n ≤ ⨆ via le_of_tendsto + le_ciSup on the bounded family). The degenerate n=0 term is 0 ≤ P/(2c), so the sequence-form ceiling rate_equalNoise_seq_le_wideband covers all n:ℕ (the [Nonempty ι]-guarded rate_equalNoise_le_wideband only bounded n≥1).

Wideband rate g(t)=(t/2)log(1+a/t) is STRICTLY CONCAVE in the bandwidth/channel-count variable t>0: second derivative g''(t) = -a^2/(2 t (t+a)^2) < 0. Complements the existing strict-monotonicity (rate_equalNoise_count_strictMonoOn); together they pin the wideband capacity curve as strictly increasing + strictly concave + asymptotic to P/(2c) from below. Distinct from the power-concavity in Concave.lean (parallelRate_concaveOn_power).

Lean gotcha: HasDerivAt.div/HasDerivAt.sub emit Pi.div/Pi.sub function forms ((fun _=>a)/(fun s=>s+a)); 'convert ... using 1' then spawns a spurious AddCommGroup instance-equality goal. Fix: annotate intermediate HasDerivAt with the pointwise lambda type (forces defeq) and close by rewriting the target derivative value then 'exact hhalf' instead of convert.

Lean gotcha: field_simp makes NO progress when a denominator is a bare SUM like (1 + a/t) (cannot prove a sum != 0 structurally). Rewrite 1 + a/t = (t+a)/t (add_div + div_self) first so only atomic denominators t, t+a remain.

parallelRate is jointly STRICTLY concave in the power vector on the nonnegative orthant, not merely weakly concave: distinct allocations differ in some coordinate whose per-channel term is strictly concave, the rest weakly concave, so Finset.sum_lt_sum gives a strict sum inequality. This upgrades water-filling from a global optimum to THE unique global optimum.

The water-filling capacity value function C(P) is CONCAVE in the scalar total power budget for a general (non-equal) noise profile — proved via feasibility of the convex-combination allocation (waterfilling_optimal) + joint vector concavity (parallelRate_concaveOn_power), no envelope theorem. Previously only the equal-noise special case and vector/bandwidth concavity existed.
